Only a trusted click counts, and two clicks less than a paint apart produce no entry. The `navigate` step drives one; `visitDocument` (pushState from script) never does. `navigationsWithoutSoftNavigation` (`runner/session/steps.ts`) names the `navigate` labels Chrome recorded no soft navigation for.

+`--mode softnav` runs scenarios that declare a `softNav` plan (`softNav`, in `scenarios/softNav.ts`). A session boots once on the structure tool's root list, then runs the plan's `navigate` steps, six passes of: the root list to the post list (`pane-open`), the list to a post (`document-open`), that post to the next one in the list (`document-switch`), and the structure tool to the empty tool (`tool-switch`). Each pass opens two posts it has not opened before. After a document open the runner waits for the form to turn editable, and after every step it drains the collector, which also spaces the clicks more than a paint apart. The way back to the structure tool goes through the router: a trusted click on the structure tool's navbar link records no soft navigation in Chromium 156, so it cannot be a measured step.
+`stats/softNav.ts` measures every soft navigation in its `navigationId` bucket, the way web-vitals does with `reportSoftNavs`:
+- **soft LCP time**: the largest paint credited to the navigating click, across all drains, measured from the click.
+- **soft FCP time**: the soft navigation entry's `duration`.
+- **soft INP latency**: the worst interaction in the bucket. The navigating click carries the previous `navigationId`, so it is moved to the navigation it started.
+- **soft CLS score**: the worst session window of shifts without recent input.

+A session fails when the navigate steps and the soft navigations do not pair up one to one (`sample-count-mismatch`, naming the steps without an entry), or when a document open's soft LCP paints before the document's data is on screen or lands on pane chrome (`paint-attribution`). The second check guards the mock: data the browser does not credit to the click would make soft LCP measure the pane skeleton instead. Studio swaps the title element as the form turns editable, so Chrome often reports the LCP element as detached; the timing check still applies then.
+The step labels are finer than the `change` kinds Studio's soft-navigation telemetry sends. Compare lab and field data through this mapping:
+`click to ready` has no field counterpart. It is a lab cross-check on how far a navigation's soft LCP sits from the moment the destination is ready.

+Every row is labelled `nav:<step label> / <metric>`, e.g. `nav:document-open / soft LCP time`. The separator is plain ASCII because labels end up in CLI arguments, GROQ and URLs. Labels never end in `LCP`, `FCP`, `INP` or `CLS`, which Radar reads as hard-navigation vitals. Each session's per-navigation values stay one array, so the session is the bootstrap unit and repeated navigations never count as independent samples. The mode runs absolute only and rejects `--reference-dist`: on identical builds the reference side ran 5-10% slower on every soft-navigation metric, whichever side went first.

1. Schema: `studio/schemas/<name>.ts` exporting a workspace partial; register in `sanity.config.ts`.

-2. Scenario: `scenarios/<name>.ts` via `defineScenario` — deterministic fixture (use `scenarios/fixtures/prng.ts`, never `Math.random`), `interactions` (fields to type into; `kind: 'pte'` for Portable Text; `readbackText` if the value isn't a plain string at the field path), seeded image assets if needed (`cdn.sanity.io/images/*` is served a constant PNG by the route guard). For INP mode a scenario may declare `steps` (`runner/session/steps.ts`): a choreography of `type` / `click` / `navigate` / `hover` / `awaitVisible` / `scroll` / `press` steps over `{field}` / `{testId}` / `{label}` / `{css}` selectors, run to completion each pass, with `raw` as the escape hatch and an optional `readback` per step checked against the mock store. Without `steps`, INP mode types into each interaction target in turn. A `navigate` step is a soft navigation: it clicks the target, waits in-page until the URL has changed and matches `url` and the `ready` CSS selector is visible (`readyWhen: 'filled'` also waits for its value or text), and records `bench:navigate:<label>` from the click's event timestamp to that point. For soak mode a scenario may declare `soak` (see [Soak mode](#soak-mode-long-session)): a typing target, excursions built from the same steps (plus `visitDocument`), a seed, an optional settle minute and live presence. For pageload mode a scenario may declare `load: {steps}`, run once per load from navigation start: `awaitVisible` and `click` steps can carry a `milestone` name, recorded as a report-only `<condition> · <milestone>` row (a `click` milestone marks when the target became clickable, via a trial click), and `awaitEditable` is the keystroke probe behind the gated `time to editable` row. Without `load`, pageload waits for the readiness selector and then probes `interactions[0]`. JS chunks and auth trips are counted up to the later of editable and the last milestone. `load.auth: 'logged-out'` boots with no stored token against a mock that signs in only requests carrying the bench token (`setRequireToken`, answered by `mock-api/auth.ts`; `/users/me` returns 200 `{}` like the e2e auth helpers), so the studio shows its login screen. A click on the provider link hits the route guard's fake provider, which redirects back with `#sid=`; the mock's `/auth/fetch` exchanges it for the token. `load.conditions` limits which load conditions are sampled, e.g. cold only when a login would leave a token for the warm page to inherit. Authenticated scenarios are unaffected: the mock signs in every request unless a scenario asks for a token. Pageload also fails a session on unexpected mock endpoints, as interaction mode does.
